answer.answer:
Ranked by the winter hazard sub-score across the 7 Midwest hubs:

1. **Minneapolis — 75.9** (composite 36.2, Moderate). By far the most exposed: 34.6 winter disruption days/yr, the highest observed count in the whole portfolio (rank 1), under the rule "snowfall >= 2.5 cm OR min temp <= -18.0 C". FEMA NRI long-term winter score 39.9 (WNTW 47.7, ISTM 32.0).
2. **Detroit — 43.5** (composite 25.8, Low). Only 10.4 disruption days/yr (portfolio rank 5), but the strongest NRI winter signal of these seven on paper: long-term score 63.8 (WNTW 77.1, ISTM 50.4).
3. **Chicago — 35.9** (composite 28.5, Low). 11.8 days/yr (portfolio rank 4), NRI 38.6 (WNTW 44.0, ISTM 33.3).
4. Kansas City — 30.5 (8.2 days/yr); 5. Indianapolis — 27.7 (7.0 days/yr); 6. St. Louis — 26.7 (5.2 days/yr); 7. Columbus — 26.3 (6.2 days/yr, tied with Newark on observed days).

For resilience prioritisation, Minneapolis is the clear winter case; Detroit and Chicago form a second tier where winter is also the top driver of their composite scores.
reasoning: Ranked all 7 Midwest hubs by the winter hazard sub-score.
Minneapolis leads on both observed frequency (34.6 days/yr, portfolio rank 1) and overall winter score.
Detroit ranks 2nd mainly on FEMA NRI winter components (63.8 long-term; WNTW 77.1) despite fewer observed days than Chicago.
Remaining four hubs cluster in the 26-31 range, with winter not their top composite driver.

Memphis's overall composite of 27.0 sits in the **Low** tier (rank 13 of 22). It simply leads a South group where winter scores are all modest.

What the 18.0 is made of: observed frequency contributes 60% and FEMA NRI 40%. Memphis averages **2.0 winter disruption days/yr** (2021-2025; rule: snowfall >= 2.5 cm OR min temp <= -18.0 C), which normalises to just 5.8 on the portfolio scale (observed-days rank 14 of 22). The NRI long-term winter score of 36.3 (WNTW 31.5, ISTM 41.1) does most of the lifting — the ice-storm component is the stronger of the two. Supporting evidence: since 2000 Memphis has had 2 Winter Storm and 2 Severe Ice Storm federal major-disaster declarations (plus 14 Severe Storm).

What actually drives Memphis is **flood (score 51.8, 10.4 points)** — 2.4 heavy-rain days/yr (>= 50 mm), observed rank 5, tied with Los Angeles, plus NRI IFLD 40.3 — and **severe storm (38.3, 7.7 points)**, where the NRI tornado component is 87.7. Those are the two hazards flagged as its top drivers; hurricane adds 3.9 points and heat 0.5.
